content:
After months of beta testing, Apple today officially launched Siri AI to the public alongside iOS 27 and other operating system updates.

During the setup process, users will see a new prompt asking if they want to opt in to help improve Siri and Apple Intelligence. Here is what this option means.

Prior to today, users were asked during setup whether they wanted to help improve Siri and voice input features. If they opted in, audio and text transcripts from Siri and voice input would be shared with Apple.

Starting today, when users enable Siri AI, they will see a setup screen asking whether they want to opt in to "improve Siri and Apple Intelligence," offering two options: "Share audio and transcripts" or "Not now."

Apple says:

Improve Siri and Apple Intelligence Help improve underlying models and Siri by allowing Apple to collect and use the text and audio interactions you have with Siri, voice input, and translation features.

The thing to note here is that if you opt into this setting, the type of data Apple collects hasn't actually changed at all. What has changed is that Apple will now use this data to train and improve its underlying models, as well as for Siri and voice input as before.

Even users who previously opted in under the old settings will be asked again when they enable Siri AI. This is to give them an opportunity to reassess their choice, as the relevant data will now also be used to train Apple's underlying models.

When asking users whether they want to opt in, Apple has made its privacy safeguards clear. The company says that Siri's audio data, text transcripts, and related data will all be tied to a "random device identifier that rotates multiple times per hour." This information is not linked to your Apple Account or email address. Apple also does not use this data to build marketing profiles or sell it to anyone.

You can change your choice and toggle this feature on or off at any time via "Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements > Improve Siri and Apple Intelligence."

Apple has also published a new support document detailing these settings across all of its platforms.
